title: dsa scan report

$schema.description: JSON Schema URL for editor support.

profile.description: The design system's profile module: a path relative to this file, or a package name. See docs/architecture.md.

name.description: Human name of the design system being measured.

packages.description: Import sources that count as design-system components (exact name or package prefix).

localAliases.description: In-repo import sources that are the design system (shadcn-style owned source), e.g. @/components/ui.

tagPrefixes.description: Element tag prefixes it owns ("ck-" maps <ck-card> to Card): Angular selectors, global Vue components, web components.

mainRef.description: Ref treated as the latest core for pin currency (default origin/main, then main).

children.description: Child libraries built on the core (a product kit, a prototype). Scored on their own; they consume the core.

localAliases.description: In-repo import sources that are this library.

tagPrefixes.description: Element tag prefixes it owns ("ck-" maps <ck-card> to Card): Angular selectors, global Vue components, web components.

path.description: Folder of its code, relative to the config root (another checkout may be outside it, e.g. ../prototype).

sources.description: Folders of its code, when there are several (set by `dsa sources --pin` or Settings → Sources). Without `path` or `sources`, dsa finds them.

git.description: Clone from here when `path` is missing (or when runs are told to use remotes). Only ever read.

aliases.description: Import aliases beyond tsconfig paths, e.g. { "@/": "src/" }, relative to this folder.

exclude.description: Paths to skip inside this folder (vendored copies, generated code).

pin.description: A file holding the core commit SHA this code is pinned to; currency is then days and commits behind core's main.

owner.description: Team that owns it; findings about it are routed here.

repo.description: GitHub repo "owner/name" that receives its issues.

pin.description: A file holding the core commit SHA this code is pinned to; currency is then days and commits behind core's main.

owner.description: Team that owns it; findings about it are routed here.

repo.description: GitHub repo "owner/name" that receives its issues.

internalConsumers.description: Consumers the system team owns (docs, Storybook): scored, but not counted toward cross-consumer clusters.

include.description: Glob patterns of files to scan, relative to the config root.

by.description: What counts as one host when counting pattern spread: a file or its directory.

minOccurrences.description: Occurrences needed before a composition is more than a snowflake (rule of three).

minHosts.description: Distinct hosts needed before a composition is more than a snowflake.

minComponents.description: Minimum design-system or local components in a composition for it to be considered.

ignoreIgnoredTimes.description: A candidate ignored this many times is parked and no longer raised.

rawElements.description: Plain HTML tags that bypass the design system when written in a consumer (counted as rawElements). An element handed to a component through a prop, e.g. render={<button />}, is the system's element and isn't counted.

elementMap.description: The system's element map (which native elements it replaces, and with what), relative to the config root. Overrides the profile's.

nativeLookalikes.description: Native elements that imitate a component: { "select": "Select" }. "input[checkbox]" keys set input types. Overrides entries from the element map.

exceptionsFile.description: Each app's element-map exceptions, relative to the app. Overrides the profile's.

deprecated.description: Deprecated components and their replacements: { OldModal: Modal }.

patterns.description: Regex sources that count as a token reference in styles.

tailwind.description: Tailwind / shadcn-style systems: read classes the way the repo's own lint does.

tierLeakageSpec.description: Leak grammar shared with the repo's lint rule. Overrides the profile's.

semanticCss.description: CSS declaring --color-<name> semantic utilities. Overrides the profile's.

classNameOverrides.description: "leaky" (default): className counts as an override only when it carries drift.

arbitraryValues.description: Which arbitrary values count as drift (default color).

apps.description: Per-app switches, keyed by app or workspace name. Anything not listed is fully measured.

versions.description: Measure package versions and pin currency (default on).

components.description: Measure component use and overrides (default on).

lookalikes.description: Measure native look-alikes (default on). Usually off for Storybook.

tokenSkip.description: Files left out of token compliance, globs relative to the app.

start.description: How to start the app for screenshots, e.g. "npm run dev -- --port {port}".

url.description: URL once started; {port} is filled in.

routes.description: Pages to visit; replaces the routes found in the source.

extraRoutes.description: Pages visited first, added to the ones found in the source.

flows.description: Written-down UI sequences that reveal elements only a filled field or an upload shows.

screenshots.description: false: never start this app for screenshots.

threshold.description: Below this confidence a human decides (default 0.9).

labPaths.description: Specimen pages, globs relative to each app. Overrides the profile's.

decisionsFile.description: Each app's review decisions, relative to the app. Overrides the profile's.

rendered.description: Rendered signatures measured in the system's Storybook (the review add-on).

useStatic.description: Measure the static Storybook build instead of starting Storybook.

shots.description: App screenshots for element review (the review add-on).

reveal.description: Open menus, tabs and sheets to find hidden elements (default on).

modules.description: Optional modules. Off modules keep their settings; they just don't run.

defaultRepo.description: Repo that receives findings whose owner has none.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone for dates in the report, e.g. "America/Los_Angeles".

value.description: The deployed commit SHA, when the deploy step writes it into the config.

env.description: Environment variables that hold the deployed commit (default: the common CI ones, such as GITHUB_SHA and CI_COMMIT_SHA). false: don't read them.

endpoint.description: A URL on the live site that reports its version (JSON or text), e.g. https://example.com/version.json.

field.description: Where the commit is in the endpoint's JSON, as a dotted path (default: sha, commit, revision, version or git.sha).

liveAtField.description: Where the time it went live is in the endpoint's JSON (default: deployedAt, builtAt, time or timestamp).

liveAt.description: When this revision went live (ISO time), if the deploy step knows it.

sources.description: The order to try revision sources in. Built in: "value", "endpoint", "env"; host adapters add their own (the GitHub one adds "github-deployment").

environment.description: For a host adapter's deployment source: the environment name (GitHub: default "github-pages").

onMismatch.description: When the checkout isn't the live revision (another commit, or uncommitted changes): refuse to run, or run and label the report loudly.

apps.description: Per app, where its live version is. Apps not listed are started from the checkout as before, and labelled.

url.description: The deployed URL, e.g. https://example.com/app/. Used as is: nothing is started.

dir.description: The built output folder that is deployed (dist, storybook-static), relative to the config root. dsa serves it on localhost for the run.

base.description: With `dir`: the path the folder is mounted at on the live site, e.g. "/app/" (default "/").

auth.description: A saved sign-in (browser storage state) for `url`, made once with `dsa login <url>`. Relative to the config root. Never commit it.

readApi.description: Let the screenshot crawler read (GET) the site's own /api/ routes, so signed-in pages load their data. Writes stay blocked. Default on for `url`, off for `dir`.

app.description: Shorthand for every app without its own entry in `apps`.

url.description: The deployed URL, e.g. https://example.com/app/. Used as is: nothing is started.

dir.description: The built output folder that is deployed (dist, storybook-static), relative to the config root. dsa serves it on localhost for the run.

base.description: With `dir`: the path the folder is mounted at on the live site, e.g. "/app/" (default "/").

storybook.description: Where the system's live Storybook is: a deployed URL or the built storybook-static folder.

url.description: The deployed URL, e.g. https://example.com/app/. Used as is: nothing is started.

dir.description: The built output folder that is deployed (dist, storybook-static), relative to the config root. dsa serves it on localhost for the run.

base.description: With `dir`: the path the folder is mounted at on the live site, e.g. "/app/" (default "/").

readApi.description: Let the screenshot crawler read (GET) the site's own /api/ routes, so signed-in pages load their data. Writes stay blocked. Default on for `url`, off for `dir`.

live.description: What is live in production. With this set, runs check the checkout against the live revision and screenshots come from the live site.

adapter.description: Which host adapter turns the static dashboard's actions into requests: "generic" or "github" (add-ons may add more).

base.description: The sub-path the dashboard is served under, e.g. "/dsa/" (default "/"). Used by dsa serve; dsa publish writes relative links that work under any path.

url.description: Where people open the dashboard, e.g. https://example.com/dsa/. Shown in issues and messages.

rescan.description: The static dashboard's Re-scan button (generic adapter).

url.description: Where Re-scan goes: a page that starts the scan job (opened in a new tab), or a webhook (POSTed to).

decisions.description: Where decisions made on the static dashboard go.

mode.description: export: download a file; post: send it to `url`; issue / pr (the github adapter): file it as an issue that a workflow applies, committing it (issue) or opening a pull request (pr). Default: the adapter's (generic export, github issue).

url.description: For post: the webhook that receives the decisions file.

repo.description: The repo "owner/name" whose workflow re-scans and receives decisions (default: github.defaultRepo).

workflow.description: The workflow file that runs the scan (needs a workflow_dispatch trigger).

ref.description: The branch the workflow runs on (default: the repo's default branch).

label.description: The label on decision issues, which the apply workflow listens for.

server.description: GitHub's web address (GitHub Enterprise Server: your host).

api.description: GitHub's API address (default https://api.github.com, or <server>/api/v3 for a server).

host.description: How the dashboard is hosted: the sub-path, and what its Re-scan and decision buttons do when it is a static site.

adapter.description: Where run history and the data folder persist between runs: "local" (stays in the data folder), "git-branch", or "command" (your own pull and push commands, e.g. for an object store).

branch.description: git-branch: the branch that holds the data folder.

remote.description: git-branch: the remote to fetch from and push to.

keep.description: git-branch: keep every push as a commit, or keep the branch at one commit (smaller; force-pushes the data branch).

pull.description: command: the shell command that restores the data folder ({dir} is filled in).

push.description: command: the shell command that saves it ({dir} is filled in).

exclude.description: Data folder entries never persisted, on top of secrets.json, auth/, site/ and report/.

history.description: Where run history (the DuckDB file) and the rest of the data folder persist between runs.

settings.description: Rule settings on top of the metric catalog's defaults.

baseline.description: Path of the correct-use baseline, relative to the config root.

dir.description: Directory the CLI writes JSON reports to, relative to the config root.

description: Output of `dsa scan`: inventory, adoption (definition 1: imports) and correct-use findings.
